fullPassage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ created → creating: 명사 scholars를 수식하는 현재분사 creating
det.analysis:

✅ ② working: 'professionals working in educational technology'에서 명사 수식 현재분사 — 적절

❌ ③ created → creating: 'some scholars creating digital projects'에서 scholars를 수식하는 현재분사 creating이 필요. created(과거/과거분사)는 능동으로 만드는 의미를 나타내지 못해 오류 ← 정답

✅ ④ keep: 'we should always keep'에서 조동사 should 뒤 동사원형 — 적절
det.tip: 명사 + 현재분사(scholars creating). created(X, 수동/완료 불일치)

questions.passage: Over the last several decades, scholars have developed standards for how best to create, organize, present, and preserve digital information for future generations. What has remained neglected for the most part, however, are the needs of people with disabilities. As a result, many of the otherwise most valuable digital resources are useless for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as for people who are blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors. While professionals working in educational technology and commercial web design have made significant progress in meeting the needs of <u>such users</u>, some scholars creating digital projects all too often fail to take these needs into account. This situation would be much improved if more projects embraced the idea that we should always keep the largest possible audience in mind as we make design decisions, ensuring that our final product serves the needs of those with disabilities as well as those without.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 such users가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① such users는 앞에 언급된 청각·시각 장애가 있는 사람들을 가리킴
det.analysis:
✅ ① 청각·시각 장애가 있는 사람들: 'have made significant progress in meeting the needs of such users'에서 such users는 앞 문장의 'people who are deaf or hard of hearing ... blind, have low vision, or have difficulty distinguishing particular colors'를 가리킴 ← 정답
❌ ② 디지털 프로젝트를 만드는 학자들: 학자는 요구를 고려하는 주체
❌ ③ 교육 기술 전문가들: 전문가는 요구를 충족시키는 주체
❌ ④ 미래 세대의 어린 학생들: 특정 연령이 아닌 장애인을 가리킴
det.tip: such users = 앞서 언급된 청각·시각 장애가 있는 사용자들

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: those with disabilities=장애가 있는 사람들 — 최종 제품이 비장애인과 함께 요구를 충족시켜야 할 대상
det.analysis:
❌ ① only the youngest users(가장 어린 사용자만): 모든 사용자 포함과 반대
❌ ② future generations alone(미래 세대만): 특정 집단만은 논지와 반대
✅ ③ those with disabilities(장애가 있는 사람들): 원문 일치. 최종 제품이 '장애가 있는 사람들'과 그렇지 않은 사람들 모두의 요구를 충족시켜야 한다는 맥락에 부합 ← 정답
❌ ④ only paying customers(돈 내는 고객만): 모든 사용자 포함과 반대
